newsitem.title: UK: UK natural gas soft in summer, firm in winter.
newsitem.headline: UK natural gas soft in summer, firm in winter.

text.p: IPE natural gas prices on Wednesday were slightly softer for the summer months while prices edged higher for the winter, dealers said.
A deal was concluded for July and August at 9.95 pence per therm, just below the psychological 10 pence mark at which the same two months were traded on Tuesday.
"The nines are good, the numbers are a little weaker today," one regular buyer said.

Dealers said the summer months had weakened partly because of expectation that Transco would sell gas under tender to be announced on Friday, following a note to this effect sent to shippers this week.
The note did not say how much gas would be involved in the sale.

Prompt prices were softer, too, and within-day gas was sold on a reasonable eneavour basis at St.Fergus at 11.00-11.10 pence per therm. This compares with within-day sales at the NBP on Tuesday of gas at 11.15-11.25 pence.
"It seems there are less people looking for gas," one dealer said.

Winter months were slightly firmer, however, and the fourth quarter of this year was traded at 13.435 and 13.40 pence per therm, compared to 13.25-13.325 on Tuesday. The first quarter of next year were traded slightly firmer at 16.75 pence per therm.
